## What this covers

How a running desktop app (GUI product) discovers a new release and swaps itself
to it, per platform, plus the operational gotchas verified during the
0.0.6 → 0.0.7-alpha end-to-end test (2026-07-10). Windows and Linux were
live-verified; mac's backend was verified with the live chip pending.

## The user-facing flow

The **UpdateChip** lives in the ChromeShell header, top-right, next to the GitHub
icon (`apps/operator/app/_components/ChromeShell.tsx` → `<UpdateChip />`).

1. It polls `GET /api/updates/manifest?target=<os>&arch=<arch>&current_version=<v>&product=gui`.
2. When a newer version resolves, the chip turns accent and reads **"Update to vX"**.
   (When up to date it's a muted "vX".)
3. Click it → confirm modal **"Install vX and restart?"** → the Rust `install_update`
   command downloads the artifact **through the operator proxy**
   `/api/updates/download` (so the GitHub token never reaches the CDN), verifies the
   **inline minisign signature**, swaps the binary, and calls `app.restart()`.
4. The relaunched app reports the new version.

**Success signal = the INSTALLED BINARY version, not the operator sidecar version.**
- Windows: the installed `papercusp-desktop.exe` FileVersion/ProductVersion.
- Linux: the AppImage file size + the header chip reading the new version after relaunch.

## Per-platform swap

| Platform | Artifact | Swap mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | `-setup.exe` (Inno/NSIS) | installer runs, replaces exe | installed exe version bumps |
| Linux | `.AppImage` | **in-place self-swap of the running AppImage** | ONLY when launched from an AppImage (`APPIMAGE` env present); else `install_update` returns `no_compatible_assets`. `.deb` gets a fallback link, not a silent update. |
| Mac | `_universal.app.tar.gz` (+`.sig`) | tar swap of the .app | universal binary, unsigned by Apple (D-002/D-006) |

Only the Linux leg exercises the AppImage self-swap path — verify it explicitly on
a Linux release, not by analogy to Windows.

## The >2GiB Linux fallback — the operational gotcha

Linux artifacts (`.AppImage`, `.deb`) run ~3–4 GB and **exceed GitHub's 2 GiB
per-asset cap**, so they are NOT uploaded as GitHub release assets. Instead:

- The release carries a small `papercusp-latest-<tag>.json` asset listing the Linux
  filename + its **inline minisign signature**.
- `/api/updates/manifest` (in `updates-manifest.ts`) first tries `pickAsset()` for a
  real GitHub asset; finding none for `linux/x86_64`, it falls back to
  `findLatestJsonAsset()` **AND** `releaseHostBase()`. **Both must be present.**
- `releaseHostBase()` (`updates-github.ts`) is simply `process.env.PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST`
  (null if unset). The proxy (`updates-download.ts`) serves `?tag=<tag>&name=<file>` by
  fetching `${host}/${tag}/${name}`, falling back to `${host}/${name}`.

**Consequence:** if the operator is launched WITHOUT `PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST`, the
manifest returns `404 no asset for linux/x86_64 (gui)` and the Linux update silently
does not appear. The fallback **code is correct**; you must **set the env var** to a
host serving the oversized artifacts. In the test rig that was
`PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST=http://10.0.2.2:8043` (host `/home/dev/release-host-8043/desktop-v<tag>/`).
**Real Linux installs need this baked into the shipping operator env** — tracked as a
follow-up (WI-3875, still open as of 2026-07-11 — blocked on an owner decision for the
production release-host URL; no hosting infra exists in-repo yet). `latest.json` is
generated for the **GUI product only**; a Server-role artifact must never land in it.
(WI-3696, **fixed** 2026-07-10: `release-local.sh`'s generator previously last-one-wins
overwrote the darwin/windows GUI entries with the Server artifact + its still-VALID
signature — a silent wrong-product swap. The fix skips any `Server`-named artifact before
classification and adds a cut-time assertion that every emitted entry's URL contains
`GUI`, failing loudly instead of shipping a bad manifest.)

## Two field gotchas that cost time

1. **WebKitGTK ignores synthetic KEY events.** On the Linux webview, `xdotool`
   F5 / ctrl+r / typing do nothing — the update chip and confirm modal must be
   driven with **MOUSE events (mousemove/click)** only. Mouse works; keys don't.

2. **The onboarding screen hides the whole ChromeShell header — including the
   UpdateChip.** `/` redirects to `/onboarding` until
   `/api/desktop/setup-wizard-state` has a `finished_at` timestamp. If the chip is
   missing, the app is on onboarding: confirm `finished_at` is set (or click
   "Launch setup" → OnboardingConsole's graduation poll auto-navigates home once
   graduated). A cold-boot race can leave the webview idle even with `finished_at`
   set — the "Launch setup" click unsticks it.

## Safety boundary for Update / Revert E2E

Never run the destructive updater/revert flow from a copied host home under
Xvfb. A copied `operator.json`, heartbeat, console marker, socket, or embedded
database can contain PIDs that name unrelated live processes on the host. On
2026-07-16 that pattern ended three graphical sessions by signaling the live
user systemd process group.

The canonical Linux route is the existing clean-room VM:

```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
PAPERCUSP_E2E_RELEASE_HOST=http://10.0.2.2:8043 \
  ./vmctl updater-e2e /path/to/Papercusp-baseline.AppImage
./vmctl gui updater
```

The command resets a dedicated overlay, proves the guest boot ID differs from
the host, copies only the AppImage, launches with an empty guest `HOME`, and
validates the new `operator.json` process-birth identity against guest `/proc`.
Update and Revert are then driven inside the SPICE guest. Host `.papercusp`
state is never an input to this test.

## Cutting a release the updater will accept

- Tags are `desktop-v<semver>-<channel>` (e.g. `desktop-v0.0.7-alpha`).
  `updates-manifest.ts` normalizes `desktop-v…` → semver; the tauri updater compares
  semver (NOT `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, which is cosmetically "dev" and only shows in the
  footer). Channel is read from the operator's stored `update_channel` (the test VMs
  use `alpha`).
- Signatures must be the **inline `.sig` CONTENT** (minisign), served in the manifest
  `signature` field — a URL to a `.sig` does not work.
- Sign via the `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` env var, never `--private-key` on argv
  (argv echoes the key into build logs — WI-3823).
